_meta.purpose: Hand-set inputs to log_miner.py's turn->project attribution. Kept as a script INPUT (the qualitative-ratings.json pattern from WS-X) so a re-run cannot silently overwrite an adjudicated call, and so every judgment carries its reason in the published record.
_meta.how_used: log_miner.py attributes a turn by folder, then by content (RULE P: explicit foreign project path; RULE S: >=2 foreign markers and 0 own). `windows` bounds which project a turn CAN be re-attributed to at a given date; `overrides` settles individual turns the rules get wrong. All 18 rule-fired re-attributions in the first pass were hand-read before this file was written.

windows._note: A turn can only be re-attributed to project X if its timestamp falls inside X's window. Dates are inclusive; null end = open. The windows exist because three corpus projects were EXTRACTED from btest and one was designed weeks before its first commit - so 'this turn mentions smim' does not mean 'this turn belongs to the smim repo' when smim was still a package inside btest.

btest.reason: First commit. Owns all SMIM work before 2026-05-02 and all EODHD tooling work before 2026-07-09, because those trees lived inside btest until they were extracted.

b-autobot.reason: Bootstrap prompt in history 2026-03-03; git span 2026-03-05..03-11; nothing after March. Bounded end stops later 'cucumber/maven' chatter from being read as b-autobot work.

blive.reason: First commit 2026-04-26 (the day claude.ai authored Requirements v0). End extended past the last commit (2026-06-06) because the method paper continued to live in blive/docs/method/paper into July.

smim.reason: Standalone repo created 2026-05-02 (single squashed commit). Before that date SMIM was src/quantdsl_backtest/smim inside btest, so its turns are btest's - this is what blocked four March/April false positives.

harp.reason: Repo created 2026-04-08 out of btest (the creation prompt itself was typed in the btest folder). Open end: the paper went to arXiv/SSRN in June, well after the last commit.

datacli.reason: Extracted from btest 2026-07-09 (btest commit 5e8cd8f). Raw EODHD snapshots stay in btest, so datacli sessions legitimately run in the btest folder.

seamQ.reason: claude.ai handoff/kickoff artifacts dated 2026-04-30 precede the first commit (2026-05-16) by over two weeks (OQ-2). The git span is not the project span.

overrides.match_preview: oh no we are just starting:).. so let's do this now study this strategy also using dsl but its in a notebook
overrides.reason: RULE P false positive. The turn cites a btest notebook path as INPUT; the deliverable is blive's (paper-account milestone for the first live-trading candidate). Citing another project's artifact is not doing that project's work.
RULE P false positive, same shape: harp supplies the residuals and block partition, seamQ implements the frame-incompatibility diagnostic. The deposit lands in seamQ.

adjudication_log.reason: 2026-03-20 .. 2026-04-05: docs/smim/, quantdsl_backtest.smim.profiling, [SMIM GPU-0.1] commit tags - all btest-internal paths from the era when SMIM was a btest package.
2026-04-08 is harp's own creation prompt ('copy what is needed into the new empty repo here .../harp'), typed from the btest folder; 2026-04-15 is harp journal strategy. Both are harp work.
2026-07-11, after the 2026-07-09 extraction; the `eodhd>` shell is datacli's. datacli sessions run in the btest folder because the raw snapshots stayed there.
2026-07-14, reading blive/docs/method/paper - the method-paper draft in blive's tree.
The eval repo's own sessions discuss every corpus project by construction; re-attributing them would inject meta-research turns into the projects being measured.
Copilot sessions attributed to harp by raw path-hit counting (WS0's session-level method) whose actual briefs are btest EODHD work. Turn-level attribution is strictly better here.
